clue.text: Fugitive from East, spy without cover

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the spy word is wrapped round the cover word

parts.note: to spy is to see or catch sight of
a cap is a cover or lid, as on a bottle or pen

explanation.surface: A runaway from the East is a secret agent whose cover has been blown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: SEE goes round CAPE to give SCAPEE, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has broken out of custody is a runaway on the loose.

clue.text: Net cunningly, prior to criminal charge

definitions.text: Net cunningly, prior to criminal charge

indicators.note: done cunningly suggests the letters of the word net are artfully rearranged

parts.note: a rap is slang for a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: A police trap sprung slyly just before someone is charged.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue describes the answer as well as building it, with 'cunningly' rearranging the net.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone into committing a crime so they can be caught is to snare them by trickery.

clue.text: Large animal or a cub I found wandering

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so the words or a cub I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big beast or a young bear I came across roaming about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges ORACUBI; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American reindeer is a sizeable deer of the tundra.

clue.text: Fix journey up, working for agency's founder

parts.note: to fix something in place is to pin it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word journey's synonym is written bottom to top

parts.note: a trek is a long journey
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: Arrange a trip north while working for a firm's founding father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TREK into KERT in this down entry. Allan Pinkerton founded the famous American detective agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Allan Pinkerton set up the National Detective Agency in Chicago in the 1850s.

clue.text: Riders a squire sent all over the place

indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place are jumbled, so a squire sent is rearranged

explanation.surface: Horsemen a country gentleman dispatched in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges ASQUIRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: People on horseback are horsemen and horsewomen.

clue.text: Father's dancing in place of uncle

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, with the possessive s
a hop is an informal dance, so dancing gives hop

explanation.surface: Dad's out boogieing instead of his brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, and 'pop' means to pawn, so a pawnshop is the place of uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is slang for a pawnbroker, whose premises were nicknamed after pawning goods.

clue.text: Sort of jacket in a shade of green

definitions.meaning: a short double-breasted sailor's coat is a ... jacket
... green is a soft yellowish-green colour

explanation.definitionFit: Both the sailor's reefer coat and the pale green colour take this word as their first part.

clue.text: Trouble with duck? Sauce is the answer

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance or trouble
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A cook troubled by a duck dish finds the sauce solves the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is the answer' just links the definition to the wordplay. O is a cricket duck, a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genoese basil, pine-nut and parmesan mixture is a classic pasta sauce.

clue.text: In this case, one's arm may be supported

definitions.text: In this case, one's arm may be supported

parts.words: In this case, one's arm may be supported
parts.note: reads like a sling for an injured limb, but arm means a firearm and case is the leather pouch carrying it

explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is carried in a leather case worn at the hip or shoulder.

clue.text: Priggish person's rubbish-collecting project

indicators.note: collecting means the priggish person takes in the rubbish word

parts.note: a prude is a priggish, easily shocked person
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A prim do-gooder's scheme for gathering litter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' signals the container; 'project' is a verb, to stick out, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to jut or stick out beyond a surface.

clue.text: Dancing was supposed to follow after this bit

definitions.text: Dancing was supposed to follow after this bit

parts.words: Dancing was supposed to follow after this bit
parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite: the frenzied Italian tarantella dance was once thought to cure, or follow, a spider's bite

explanation.definitionFit: In southern Italian folklore, the bite of a large wolf spider caused a mania cured by frantic dancing.

clue.text: Girl with endless promise gets round of applause

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally

indicators.note: endless means the promise word loses its final letter

parts.note: a vow is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: A young woman who keeps breaking her word still gets an ovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from VOW to leave VO.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of simultaneous gunfire, and by extension a burst of cheering.

clue.text: Slow pace of punt heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the punt synonym is removed

parts.note: to punt is to bet, to gamble

explanation.surface: A leisurely speed for a flat boat with its pole gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like the boat but is a bet; 'heading off' drops the G of GAMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll or leisurely walk is an unhurried pace.

clue.text: Fan smashing bottles left

indicators.note: bottles means the smashing word holds the left word inside it

parts.note: smashing means excellent, super
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A football fan breaking the bottles that were left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun but is the verb, to hold inside, signalling the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is a follower or backer of a team or cause.

clue.text: Diligent one in vessel, venturing

indicators.note: in means the one letter is put inside the vessel word

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
I is the Roman numeral for one
staking money is venturing or risking it

explanation.surface: A hard-working sailor aboard ship, setting out boldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking great care and effort over work is being thorough and careful.

clue.text: Unlikely to catch leader of bandits, say, identified as criminal

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of bandits

parts.note: to utter is to say
to finger someone is slang for identifying them to the police as a culprit

explanation.surface: A gang chief named by informers is not likely to get away, or be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: B (leader of bandits) + UTTER + FINGERED. In the definition 'catch' is about holding a ball, not arresting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone clumsy who keeps dropping things, especially a fielder, is not likely to hold a catch.

clue.text: Appealing to partner to make our slam go off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of our slam go are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bridge player urges a partner to bid so the grand slam comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' reads as succeed, but 'off' rearranges OURSLAMGO. A slam in bridge is a bid to win all or all but one trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attractive and alluring has glitz and charm.

clue.text: Writer discharging first round to shoot game

indicators.note: round means what is left of the writer goes around the shoot word
discharging first means the writer word drops its opening letter

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist
to bag game is to shoot it

explanation.surface: An author fires his first round to shoot some game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharging first' and 'shoot' sound like gunfire, but they drop a letter and give BAG; 'round' signals the container, leaving CRIBE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a card game scored with pegs on a board.

clue.text: Scouting revival needs to include kid

indicators.note: to include means the revival word takes the kid word inside it

parts.note: a renaissance is a revival or rebirth
to kid is to fool or con

explanation.surface: A reinvigorated Scout movement must take in children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' signals the container, with 'needs' a link. 'Kid' is the verb, to deceive, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Military surveying of enemy ground is a scouting mission.

clue.text: Cop failing to end entirely derisive noise

indicators.note: failing to end means the cop word loses its final letter

parts.note: to cop is to catch
all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A policeman who never finishes the job is roundly jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop' looks like a policeman but is the verb; 'failing to end' drops the H from CATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or jeer of disapproval is a mocking sound.

clue.text: Poor char outside used to be saloon's cleaner?

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters go round the used to be word
poor suggests the word char is in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
was is the past tense of be, used to be

explanation.surface: A badly paid cleaning lady once kept a bar clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges CHAR to CARH, which goes 'outside' WAS. A saloon is a British car body style, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a sedan car, and the drive-through washing station cleans cars.

clue.text: Beset when on voyage

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
to sail is to voyage

explanation.surface: Troubled while out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set upon or attacked from all sides is to be assaulted.

clue.text: Willow trees transformed a part of London'

parts.note: cricket bats are made of willow, so willow can stand for a bat

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of trees and a are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Willow trees altered a London neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges TREESA to TERSEA. BATTERSEA is a district of south London on the Thames, known for its power station and dogs' home.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a district on the south bank of the Thames in London.

clue.text: Duck with bright colour that is showing up

indicators.note: showing up in a down entry means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: red is a bright colour
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A duck with gaudy plumage that stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: REDIE read 'showing up' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large sea duck prized for its soft down.

clue.text: Giants held back by lesser gods

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Titans restrained by minor deities.
explanation.walkthrough: SERGO sits in 'lesser gods'; 'held back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are monstrous man-eating giants of fairy tale.

clue.text: Give notice that conflict must stop

indicators.note: must stop treats the notice as a stopper plugging the conflict word inside it

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: An ultimatum announcing that hostilities must cease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must stop' signals the container, picturing a plug; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a prize or grant is to bestow it formally.

clue.text: Terriers after drink grabbing fruit and sausage

indicators.note: after means the terriers come behind the drink-and-fruit piece
grabbing means the drink word takes hold of the fruit word inside it

parts.note: cola is a fizzy drink
a hip is the fruit of the rose
the Territorial Army, whose soldiers are nicknamed terriers, is TA

explanation.surface: Dogs after a drink snatch some fruit and a banger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terriers' are part-time soldiers of the British Territorial Army, not dogs; 'grabbing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage.

clue.text: It's used when potting in gardens, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool used for potting plants at Kew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potting' suggests potting plants, but it is potting balls in snooker or pool. KEW is London's famous botanic gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooker player strikes the ball into a pocket with a long tapered stick.

clue.text: Learn curiously, for example about wax

indicators.note: curiously means oddly arranged, so the letters of learn are rearranged
about means the for example abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Study the odd case of candle wax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' turns LEARN into ENLAR; 'about' reverses EG to GE. 'wax' is the verb, as the moon waxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to grow larger, as the moon does.

clue.text: Note, in the can, fuel

indicators.note: in means the note goes inside the prison word

parts.note: the can is slang for prison, gaol
soh is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A message left in the lavatory about petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the can' is slang for prison (GAOL, British spelling of jail), not a tin or toilet. GASOHOL is petrol blended with alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of petrol and ethyl alcohol is burned in engines.
